Let \(K=\mathbb F_{p^2}\). Every subfield \(E\subset M_4(\mathbb F_p)\) of order \(p^2\) makes \(\mathbb F_p^4\) into a \(2\)-dimensional \(K\)-vector space. Thus all such subfields are conjugate.

For such a field \(E\), its trace-zero elements form a \(1\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-line. Indeed, if \(x\in K\), its matrix trace on \(\mathbb F_p^4\) is
\[
2\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb F_p}(x),
\]
and \(p\) is odd. Hence \(E\) is determined by any nonzero trace-zero element \(X\in E\), and such an \(X\) satisfies
\[
X^2=dI
\]
for some nonsquare \(d\in\mathbb F_p^\times\).

So the problem is equivalent to counting ordered triples of trace-zero lines \([X_1],[X_2],[X_3]\), with \(X_i^2\) a nonsquare scalar, such that
\[
X_iX_j=-X_jX_i
\]
for \(i\ne j\).

First count all fields \(E\subset M_4(\mathbb F_p)\) of order \(p^2\). The stabilizer of one fixed copy of \(K\) is
\[
\operatorname{GL}_2(K)\rtimes \operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb F_p),
\]
so the number is
\[
N_1=\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|}{2|\operatorname{GL}_2(K)|}.
\]

Fix \(E_1\), and choose \(X=X_1\) with \(X^2=dI\), \(d\) nonsquare. A matrix \(Y\) anticommutes with \(X\) iff \(Y\) is \(K/\mathbb F_p\)-semilinear with respect to the nontrivial automorphism of \(K\). Thus
\[
Y=C\sigma,\qquad C\in \operatorname{GL}_2(K),
\]
and
\[
Y^2=C\overline C.
\]
We need \(Y^2=eI\) with \(e\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) nonsquare. For each fixed nonsquare \(e\), the number of \(C\) with \(C\overline C=eI\) equals
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(K)|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|},
\]
by the usual Hilbert-90 count \(C=P^{-1}\overline P\), whose fibers are right cosets of \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)\). Since there are \((p-1)/2\) choices of nonsquare \(e\), and each field is counted \(p-1\) times by its nonzero trace-zero generators,
\[
N_2=\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(K)|}{2|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}.
\]

Now fix \(X,Y\) with \(X^2=dI\), \(Y^2=eI\), both \(d,e\) nonsquares, and \(XY=-YX\). The algebra generated by \(X,Y\) is \(M_2(\mathbb F_p)\), so its centralizer in \(M_4(\mathbb F_p)\) is another copy of \(M_2(\mathbb F_p)\). Any \(Z\) anticommuting with both \(X\) and \(Y\) has the form
\[
Z=XYC,\qquad C\in M_2(\mathbb F_p).
\]
Then
\[
Z^2=(XY)^2C^2=-de\,C^2.
\]
Since \(de\) is a square, \(Z^2\) is a nonsquare scalar iff
\[
C^2=cI,\qquad \chi(c)=-\chi(-1),
\]
where \(\chi\) is the quadratic character of \(\mathbb F_p^\times\).

Count such \(C\in M_2(\mathbb F_p)\).

If \(c\) is a square, \(C\) is either one of the two scalar matrices \(\pm \sqrt c\,I\), or conjugate to \(\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt c,-\sqrt c)\). Thus for each square \(c\),
\[
p(p+1)+2
\]
matrices occur.

If \(c\) is a nonsquare, \(t^2-c\) is irreducible, and the conjugacy class has centralizer \(\mathbb F_{p^2}^\times\), so for each nonsquare \(c\) there are
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}{p^2-1}=p(p-1)
\]
matrices.

Therefore the number of possible third fields is
\[
N_3=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{p(p-1)}2, & p\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\[6pt]
\dfrac{p(p+1)+2}{2}, & p\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
\]

Hence the required number is
\[
N_1N_2N_3
=
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|}{4|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}N_3.
\]
Since
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}
=p^5(p^3-1)(p^4-1),
\]
the final answer is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{p^6(p-1)(p^3-1)(p^4-1)}{8}, & p\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\[8pt]
\dfrac{p^5(p^2+p+2)(p^3-1)(p^4-1)}{8}, & p\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}}
\]
